Name: NAT-T: ESP-in-UDP Encapsulation Active in Kernel XFRM State
Description: Verifies NAT Traversal by inspecting the kernel XFRM SA directly with 'ip xfrm state show'. With forceencaps=yes, the kernel installs the SA with encap type espinudp on port 4500, regardless of whether actual NAT is present. This simulates a real-world SD-WAN deployment where ESP (protocol 50) is blocked.

Name: Ping Site A LAN → Site B LAN (0% packet loss)
Description: Sends 4 ICMP echo requests from Site A's LAN IP (100.64.1.1) to Site B's LAN IP (100.64.2.1) through the VPN tunnel. Source is pinned to 100.64.1.1 via -I to match the leftsubnet policy and trigger XFRM encryption.

Name: IKE Phase 2 — Child SA (ESP) is INSTALLED in Kernel
Description: Verifies the IPSec Child SA (ESP) was successfully negotiated and INSTALLED into the Linux XFRM database, meaning packets will be encrypted.

Name: Ping Site B LAN → Site A LAN (bidirectional validation)
Description: Validates the reverse direction: 4 ICMP echo requests from Site B's LAN IP (100.64.2.1) to Site A's LAN IP (100.64.1.1). A one-directional pass is insufficient evidence of a healthy tunnel — both directions must work.

Name: No Plaintext ICMP Visible Between WAN IPs During Cross-Site Ping
Description: The critical encryption test: captures ICMP packets between the two WAN IPs (100.64.0.10 ↔ 100.64.0.20) while pinging. If the VPN is working correctly, zero ICMP packets should appear — all payload is encrypted inside UDP 4500. Any ICMP hit here is a security violation (traffic leak).

Name: Both Sites Independently Confirm ESTABLISHED Tunnel
Description: Validates symmetry: queries each gateway separately and asserts both report the IKE SA as ESTABLISHED. A one-sided ESTABLISHED is a misconfiguration indicator.

Name: IKE Phase 1 — SA Reaches ESTABLISHED State
Description: Queries 'ipsec statusall' on Site A and asserts the IKE SA completed the two-message IKEv2 exchange (IKE_SA_INIT + IKE_AUTH) and reached ESTABLISHED.

Name: Tunnel Covers the Correct Subnets (100.64.1.0/24 ↔ 100.64.2.0/24)
Description: Confirms the negotiated traffic selectors match the intended subnets. A wrong selector means the tunnel exists but protects the wrong traffic.

Name: UDP Port 4500 (NAT-T / ESP-in-UDP) Traffic Present on WAN During Cross-Site Ping
Description: Captures packets on the WAN interface while pinging across sites. Asserts that UDP port 4500 packets are observed, confirming the ICMP payload is wrapped inside the ESP-in-UDP (NAT-T) envelope.
